resources.string: Where you tap on each key, where your fingers drift, and which keys you correct most.

The map draws the keyboard at rest and shows, for each key, three views. Density: the spots of the key where your taps land. Learned offsets: the average shift of your taps from the key center, drawn as an arrow. Errors: the share of taps followed by a ⌫ that erased the character you had just typed. Only counters per key are kept: no text, no order of taps, no time. Nothing is counted in incognito mode, in password fields or in numeric fields. Nothing leaves the device. The erase and reset buttons of the settings also clear this map.
The brighter a spot, the more taps landed there. Each key is split into a grid of the places where your finger touched it.
Dot: the center of the key. Arrow: where your taps land on average, enlarged %1$d times to be visible. Small number: taps learned for this key.
Red: share of taps followed by a ⌫ that erased the character. Grey and a dash: fewer than %1$d taps, too few to tell. The ⌫ key itself has no error rate.

Local data: only counters per key, no text is recorded, nothing in incognito mode or in password fields. The buttons to erase them are in the settings: \"Erase learned data\" clears the tap density, \"Reset measurements\" clears the errors.
No data yet. Type a few messages and come back.
The learned touch zones and this typing map will be erased. The personal dictionary and the typing measurements are kept. This cannot be undone.
%1$s: error rate not measured for this key
